newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Short stg vol locked in by rate view.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Short stg vol locked in by rate view.

text.p: Implied volatility of short sterling options traded on LIFFE shrugged off data released earlier in the session on Friday, as traders said expectations of interest rate hikes have become entrenched in the market.

Gross domestic product in the second quarter grew by 0.9 percent, to give year-on-year growth of 3.4 percent. Although traders said the figures supported the case for a further rate increase in August, they said that expectation was already firmly in the market.
"The problem for volatility is that the market believes it is already right on the interest rate path," said a broker at a major British bank. "There's not enough doubt to drive volatility."

British base rates currently stand at 6.75 percent, following three quarter-point rises in the last three months. The short sterling strip is already discounting money market rates of just under 7.5 percent by the end of the year.
December short sterling volatility was unchanged on the previous day at 8.3 percent, with options caught between the two strikes of 92.50 at 8.7 percent and 92.75 at 7.9 percent.
December short sterling futures were down 0.01 at 92.61 by 1145 GMT.
"Volatility looks cheap, but is likely to remain there unless there is some reason for the market to revise its view of the strip," said the British bank trader.
The June 1998 short sterling options saw some call selling against the futures, with 700 lots of the 92.50 strike and 115 at 92.25.

A trader at a British brokerage said gilt options trade had been limited this session, with around 300 lots of the September calls traded at 116-00, and 1000 of the same strike in December. September volatility was at 6.25-6.75 percent, little moved from the previous session.
September gilt futures were down 2/32 at 115-09.
